arxiv-2109-03548.title: Hunting the gamma-ray emission from Fast Radio Burst with Fermi-LAT
arxiv-2109-03548.creator: on behalf of the Fermi Large Area Telescope Collaboration
arxiv-2109-03548.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by on behalf of the Fermi Large Area Telescope Collaboration. Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are one of the most exciting new mysteries of astrophysics. Their origin is still unknown, but recent observations seems to link them to Soft Gamma Repeaters and, in particular, to magnetar giant flares (MGFs). The recent detection of a MGF at GeV energies by the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) motivated the search for GeV counterparts to the > > 100 currently known FRBs.

arxiv-2205-06489.title: Joint Power Allocation and Beamformer for mmW-NOMA Downlink Systems by Deep Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2205-06489.creator: Abbas Akbarpour-Kasgari and Mehrdad Ardebilipour
arxiv-2205-06489.description: Abstract The high demand for data rate in the next generation of wireless communication could be ensured by Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) approach in the millimetre-wave (mmW) frequency band. Joint power allocation and beamforming of mmW-NOMA systems is mandatory which could be met by optimization approaches.

arxiv-2212-12493.title: Lattice calculation of the R -ratio smeared with Gaussian kernels
arxiv-2212-12493.creator: U. Wenger
arxiv-2212-12493.description: Abstract The ratio R ⁡ ( E ) R(E) of the cross-sections for e + ​ e − → e^{+}e^{-}\to hadrons and e + ​ e − → μ + ​ μ − e^{+}e^{-}\to\mu^{+}\mu^{-} is a valuable energy-dependent probe of the hadronic sector of the Standard Model.

arxiv-2304-11104.title: Approximate Shielding of Atari Agents for Safe Exploration Conference: Proc. of the Adaptive and Learning Agents Workshop (ALA 2023); May 29-30, 2023; London, UK, https://alaworkshop2023.github.io/ 60
arxiv-2304-11104.creator: Alexander W. Goodall, Francesco Belardinelli
arxiv-2304-11104.description: Abstract . Balancing exploration and conservatism in the constrained setting is an important problem if we are to use reinforcement learning for meaningful tasks in the real world. In this paper, we propose a principled algorithm for safe exploration based on the concept of shielding .

arxiv-2305-06884.title: Risk-limiting Financial Audits via Weighted Sampling without Replacement
arxiv-2305-06884.creator: Shubhanshu Shekhar, Ziyu Xu, Zachary C. Lipton, Pierre J. Liang, Aaditya Ramdas
arxiv-2305-06884.description: Abstract We introduce the notion of a risk-limiting financial auditing (RLFA): given N N transactions, the goal is to estimate the total misstated monetary fraction ( m ∗ m^{*} ) to a given accuracy ϵ \epsilon , with confidence 1 − δ 1-\delta .

arxiv-2312-08529.title: A systematic search for double eclipsing binaries in Zwicky Transient Facility data
arxiv-2312-08529.creator: T. Vaessen, J. van Roestel
arxiv-2312-08529.description: Abstract Context. Double eclipsing binaries are gravitationally bound quadruple systems in a ‘2+2’ configuration where both of the binaries are eclipsing. These systems are interesting objects to better understand stellar formation, to investigate the dynamical interaction between the two binary systems or to study certain stages of stellar evolution, such as common-envelope events or Type Ia Supernovae. Aims.

arxiv-2401-12055.title: NEUROSEC: FPGA-Based Neuromorphic Audio Security
arxiv-2401-12055.creator: Murat Isik, Hiruna Vishwamith, Yusuf Sur, Kayode Inadagbo, I. Can Dikmen
arxiv-2401-12055.description: Abstract Neuromorphic systems, inspired by the complexity and functionality of the human brain, have gained interest in academic and industrial attention due to their unparalleled potential across a wide range of applications. While their capabilities herald innovation, it is imperative to underscore that these computational paradigms, analogous to their traditional counterparts, are not impervious to security threats.

arxiv-2403-07763.title: Emerging Technologies for 6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks: From Academia to Industrial Applications
arxiv-2403-07763.creator: Cong T. Nguyen 1,2 , Yuris Mulya Saputra 3 , Nguyen Van Huynh 4 , Tan N. Nguyen 5 , Dinh Thai Hoang 6 , Diep N Nguyen 6 , Van-Quan Pham 7 , Miroslav Voznak 8 , Symeon Chatzinotas 9 , and Dinh-Hieu Tran 10
arxiv-2403-07763.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Cong T. Nguyen 1,2 , Yuris Mulya Saputra 3 , Nguyen Van Huynh 4 , Tan N. Nguyen 5 , Dinh Thai Hoang 6 , Diep N Nguyen 6 , Van-Quan Pham 7 , Miroslav Voznak 8 , Symeon Chatzinotas 9 , and Dinh-Hieu Tran 10. Terrestrial networks form the fundamental infrastructure of modern communication systems, serving more than 4 billion users globally. However, terrestrial networks are facing a wide range of challenges, from coverage and reliability to interference and congestion.

arxiv-2405-20601.title: Bayesian Nonparametric Quasi Likelihood
arxiv-2405-20601.creator: Antonio R. Linero
arxiv-2405-20601.description: Abstract A recent trend in Bayesian research has been revisiting generalizations of the likelihood that enable Bayesian inference without requiring the specification of a model for the data generating mechanism. This paper focuses on a Bayesian nonparametric extension of Wedderburn’s quasi-likelihood, using Bayesian additive regression trees to model the mean function.

arxiv-2504-01248.title: Automated Factual Benchmarking for In-Car Conversational Systems using Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-01248.creator: Rafael Giebisch, Ken E. Friedl, Lev Sorokin, Andrea Stocco
arxiv-2504-01248.description: Abstract In-car conversational systems bring the promise to improve the in-vehicle user experience. Modern conversational systems are based on Large Language Models (LLMs), which makes them prone to errors such as hallucinations, i.e., inaccurate, fictitious, and therefore factually incorrect information. In this paper, we present an LLM-based methodology for the automatic factual benchmarking of in-car conversational systems.

arxiv-2505-07625.title: QC-Adviser: Quantum Hardware Recommendations for Solving Industrial Optimization Problems
arxiv-2505-07625.creator: Djamel Laps-Bouraba, Markus Zajac, Uta Störl
arxiv-2505-07625.description: Abstract The availability of quantum hardware via the cloud offers opportunities for new approaches to computing optimization problems in an industrial environment. However, selecting the right quantum hardware is difficult for non-experts due to its technical characteristics. In this paper, we present the QC-Adviser prototype, which supports users in selecting suitable quantum annealer hardware without requiring quantum computing knowledge.

arxiv-2507-12272.title: Orbit sets, transitivity, and sensitivity with upper semicontinuous maps
arxiv-2507-12272.creator: Jeison Amorocho, Javier Camargo, Sergio Macías
arxiv-2507-12272.description: Abstract Given a compact metric space X X and an upper semicontinuous function F : X → 2 X F\colon X\to 2^{X} , we explore the dynamic system ( X , F ) (X,F) . In this study, we introduce new concepts, demonstrate various results, and provide numerous examples.

arxiv-2512-18896.title: Universal Categories
arxiv-2512-18896.creator: Hans Schoutens
arxiv-2512-18896.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hans Schoutens. The category of models of any theory T T in any first-order language L L has the surprising property that any small category that is elementarily equivalent with it, already embeds in it. The proof uses an abstract argument via ultrapowers, leaving one wonder which concrete categorical axioms, depending on T T and L L , are responsible for this embedding result. We also propose a first-order logic for which equivalent categories are always elementarily equivalent.

arxiv-2601-03671.title: NeuronScope: A Multi-Agent Framework for Explaining Polysemantic Neurons in Language Models
arxiv-2601-03671.creator: Weiqi Liu, Yongliang Miao, Haiyan Zhao, Yanguang Liu, Mengnan Du, [4pt] Wuhan University
arxiv-2601-03671.description: Abstract Neuron-level interpretation in large language models (LLMs) is fundamentally challenged by widespread polysemanticity, where individual neurons respond to multiple distinct semantic concepts. Existing single-pass interpretation methods struggle to faithfully capture such multi-concept behavior. In this work, we propose NeuronScope , a multi-agent framework that reformulates neuron interpretation as an iterative, activation-guided process.

pmc-11531327.title: Orthodontic Management of a Growing Patient With a Skeletal Class III Malocclusion and an Anterior Open Bite: A Case Report
pmc-11531327.creator: Sana Bint Aziz, Garima Arora, Gurkeerat Singh, Puneet Batra, Ashish K Singh
pmc-11531327.description: Class III malocclusion presents many challenges due to its varying elements of imbalance in skeletal, dental, and soft tissues. This necessitates a comprehensive treatment plan, including growth modification during the pre-pubertal growth phase, and long-term retention to reduce the chances of orthognathic surgery later.

pmc-12456221.title: Tyrosine kinase Cps2C regulates the synthesis of capsular polysaccharides and plays a role in the virulence of Streptococcus suis serotype 2
pmc-12456221.creator: Feng Zheng, Miao Lin, He Fang, Yuhe Wang, Qiaoqiao Wang, Xumiao Liu, Chengliang Tang, Yutao Wang, Zhuqing Shao, Hua Ni, Xiuzhen Pan
pmc-12456221.description: Streptococcus suis is a gram-positive zoonotic pathogen that causes several serious diseases in humans and various animals. Among its virulence factors, capsular polysaccharides (CPS) play a particularly pivotal role in its pathogenicity. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing CPS synthesis remain elusive.

pmc-13038260.title: Basal phosphorylation of SHIP1 by Lyn suppresses proinflammatory signaling in the absence of a phagocytic synapse
pmc-13038260.creator: S Erandika Senevirathne, William K Kanagy, Charlotte R Hemmila, Joseph T Greene, Andrew T Rajczewski, Richard T Cattley, Whitney L Swanson, Silvia Toledo Ramos, Myra G Nunez, Siyu Jin, William F Hawse, Tanya S Freedman
pmc-13038260.description: Microscale engagement of the hemi-immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif-containing receptor Dectin-1 by fungal particles activates Src-family kinases (SFKs) and Syk, drives second-messenger generation, and induces downstream Erk and Akt signaling and proinflammatory responses in macrophages. To avoid inappropriate activation in the absence of a pathogenic threat, macrophages restrict signaling in response to low-valency ligands.

pmc-13440832.title: Bridging the monitoring gap in resource-limited settings: A head-to-head evaluation of two Chinese HIV-1 RNA quantification assays and Roche TaqMan
pmc-13440832.creator: Jiafeng Zhang, Xiaobei Ding, Qin Fan, Jiezhe Yang, Yan Xia, Chengliang Chai
pmc-13440832.description: BackgroundHIV-1 RNA quantification assays are essential for evaluating antiretroviral therapy (ART) efficacy and diagnosing HIV infection, playing a pivotal role in HIV/AIDS management and treatment.MethodsThis study compares two Chinese-manufactured HIV-1 RNA quantification assays (Livzon, SymBio) with the Roche COBAS AmpliPrep/COBAS TaqMan HIV-1 Test v2.0 (reference assay) using plasma samples from 279 HIV-infected individuals.

pmc-13582774.title: Near-Peer Teaching to Integrate Anatomical Imaging into the Medical School Curriculum
pmc-13582774.creator: Andrew E Warfield, Curtis A Plante, Ryan Walsh, Abigail Hielscher
pmc-13582774.description: PurposeAdditional instruction in imaging can solidify medical students’ anatomical knowledge, which in turn, supports better clinical reasoning skills. Imaging education is often constrained due to insufficient time in the curriculum as well as instructor availability. Near-peer teaching can address some of these constraints.MethodsImaging at our school is integrated across seven anatomy blocks in the first-year curriculum.

pmc-13654093.title: A collaborative hybrid network with aggregated attention for pulmonary nodule detection
pmc-13654093.creator: Jianle Chen, Jianyu Zhu, Yiying Wang, Yuyan Lin, Huilian Liao
pmc-13654093.description: BackgroundLung cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of early detection for improving patient survival. Current imaging‑based methods for pulmonary nodule (PN) detection are often limited by low efficiency and suboptimal accuracy, falling short of the demands for precise clinical diagnosis.
